mainTopic: The limits of killing a רודף, broken vessels during a chase, and when a person must die rather than sin.
overview: The amud opens by answering a problem. A man who violates his sister pays a fine, yet someone chasing a נערה is a רודף who may be killed, and a person liable to die does not also pay. רב פפא says the fine case is a seduced girl. אביי says she could have been saved by injuring a limb, following רבי יונתן בן שאול. The גמרא proves רבי יונתן בן שאול's rule from the פסוק about men fighting who hit a pregnant woman, and backs the proof with רבא's rules about a רודף, a נרדף and a rescuer who break vessels. It then returns to the משנה: רבי שמעון בן יוחי and his son allow killing someone to stop עבודה זרה or חילול שבת. Next comes the famous vote in לוד: for any sin a person should sin rather than die, except עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים. The גמרא gives the sources for these three, including רבה's logic: who says your blood is redder? Finally, רבי יוחנן adds that in a time of persecution, or in public, one must die even for a minor מצוה. The definition of a minor מצוה begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב פפא: the fine case is a seduced girl
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה in כתובות that fines the man is talking about a girl who was seduced. In that case everyone agrees there is no רודף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the case is one of a seduced girl, and everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the contradiction. He says the case where the man pays a fine is one where the girl agreed, not one where she was forced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she agreed, nobody is chasing her and there is no רודף. Nobody may kill him to save her, so he is not liable to death at that moment, and the fine can apply. 'Everyone agrees' means this answer fits all opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who was seduced (she agreed), as opposed to forced

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is about a seduced girl, and it is the opinion of everyone.
phrases.notes: He means the כתובות case that lists the sister as getting a fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised just before this section (fine vs. רודף)
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to a seduced girl
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fine case seemed to be a forced girl, whose attacker is a רודף and liable to death
steps.terutzMaskana: The fine case is a seduced girl, so there is no רודף and the fine applies

steps.title: אביי: she could have been saved by injuring a limb
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the fine case is a forced girl, but one who could have been saved by injuring the attacker. This follows רבי יונתן בן שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the case is where one could have saved her by injuring one of his limbs, and it follows רבי יונתן בן שאול.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer. He keeps the case as a forced girl, but in a situation where she could have been rescued without killing the attacker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is possible to stop the רודף by injuring him, it is forbidden to kill him. So in that case he is not liable to death, and he can be made to pay the fine. This answer works only according to רבי יונתן בן שאול.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a case where one is able to save her by injuring one of his limbs,
and it follows Rabbi Yonatan ben Shaul.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: בְּיָכוֹל לְהַצִּיל בְּאֶחָד מֵאֵבָרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא), tied to one תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any forced girl's attacker is a רודף who may be killed, so he should not pay
steps.terutzMaskana: When she could be saved by injuring a limb, he may not be killed, so he pays the fine

steps.title: The ברייתא of רבי יונתן בן שאול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יונתן בן שאול. Someone who could have stopped a רודף by injuring a limb, but killed him instead, is executed for murder.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי יונתן בן שאול says, if a רודף was chasing someone to kill him, and one could have saved the victim by injuring one of the רודף's limbs but did not, and killed him instead, he is executed for killing him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing what רבי יונתן בן שאול holds, to back up אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Permission to kill a רודף exists only when there is no gentler way. If injuring him would have worked, killing him counts as murder. This is why, in אביי's case, the attacker is not liable to death.

keyTerms.meaning: A pursuer, someone chasing another to kill or violate them
As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יונתן בן שאול, a רודף may be killed only if he cannot be stopped by injuring him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the limit on the law of רודף: use only the least force needed.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yonatan ben Shaul says,

phrases.aramaic: רוֹדֵף שֶׁהָיָה רוֹדֵף אַחַר חֲבֵירוֹ לְהוֹרְגוֹ,
phrases.english: a pursuer who was chasing his fellow to kill him,
and one was able to save him by injuring one of his limbs,
but did not save him that way — he is executed for him.
phrases.notes: He means the rescuer killed the רודף instead of just injuring him, so he is treated as a murderer.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the opinion אביי relied on
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי יונתן בן שאול, one may not kill a רודף who can be stopped by injury
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יונתן בן שאול

steps.title: What is רבי יונתן בן שאול's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רבי יונתן בן שאול uses for his rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יונתן בן שאול?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יונתן בן שאול learns his rule from. This sets up the next step, which brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. It is a request for the Torah source behind the rule that killing a רודף who could be injured instead is murder.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yonatan ben Shaul?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן שָׁאוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for רבי יונתן בן שאול's rule

steps.title: The verse of men fighting, as explained by רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק about men fighting who hit a pregnant woman. רבי אלעזר says the fight was a fight to kill, yet the Torah still makes the striker pay for the lost fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'When men fight (together)...' And רבי אלעזר said: the פסוק is talking about a fight to kill, as it is written: 'If there is a death, you shall give a life for a life.' Even so, the Torah says: 'If there is no death, he shall surely be fined.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק and רבי אלעזר's explanation of it. These will serve as the base for proving רבי יונתן בן שאול's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר proves the men were trying to kill each other, because the Torah gives the death penalty if the woman dies. So the striker was a רודף. Still, the Torah makes him pay for the fetus, even though a person liable to death usually does not pay.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'fine' here is not for the woman's death. It is a payment for the fetus she lost, when she herself did not die.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'When men fight (together)…'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:22. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
The verse is speaking of a fight to kill,
as it is written: 'And if there is a death,'
'you shall give a life for a life.'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:23.

phrases.english: And even so, the Merciful One said:
'And there is no death, he shall surely be fined.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by bringing the פסוק and רבי אלעזר's reading
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק of men fighting: although they fought to kill, the striker is fined for the fetus

steps.title: How the fine fits if a רודף may not be killed when injury works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבי יונתן בן שאול's rule explains the פסוק. If the רודף could be stopped by a limb, he is not liable to death, so he can be fined.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say that when one can save by injuring a limb, one may not save by taking his life. That is how we find a case where the striker is fined: where it was possible to save by injuring one of his limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the proof. It shows that with רבי יונתן בן שאול's rule, we can understand why the Torah fines the striker. The next step gives the other side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The striker was a רודף, and if he could be killed he should be exempt from paying. With רבי יונתן בן שאול's rule, there is a case where killing him is forbidden: when injuring him would have stopped him. In that case he is not liable to death, so the Torah's fine makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say...
He may not be saved at the cost of the רודף's life
You can find a case for it

steps.whatToRemember: The fine in the פסוק of fighting men only makes sense if a רודף who can be stopped by injury may not be killed. This is רבי יונתן בן שאול's source.

phrases.english: It works well if you say:
when one is able to save by injuring one of his limbs,
one is not allowed to save him at the cost of the pursuer's life —
that is how you find a case where he is fined,
such as where one was able to save by injuring one of his limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the פסוק from step 5 to prove the rule of step 3
steps.raayaObject: רבי יונתן בן שאול's rule that a רודף who can be stopped by injury may not be killed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fine in שמות 21:22 for the man who struck the woman during a fight to kill

steps.title: Without this rule, the Torah's fine could never happen
steps.stepSummary: If a רודף could always be killed, he would always be liable to death and exempt from paying. Then the fine in the פסוק could never apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say that even when the victim could be saved by injuring one of the רודף's limbs, he may still be saved by killing the רודף, how could there ever be a case where the striker is fined?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from step 6 by looking at the other side. If we reject רבי יונתן בן שאול's rule, the fine in the פסוק becomes impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is liable to death for an act does not also pay money for that same act. If every רודף could be killed, the striker in the fight would always be liable to death and could never be fined. The Torah does fine him, so there must be a רודף who may not be killed: the one who could have been stopped by injuring a limb.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (if you hold the opposite view)
He may be saved at the cost of the רודף's life
How can you find such a case?
He will be fined (made to pay)

phrases.english: But if you say:
when one is able to save the victim by injuring one of the pursuer's limbs,
the victim may also be saved at the cost of the pursuer's life,
how can you find a case where he would be fined?
phrases.notes: This word comes from the פסוק about the pregnant woman (שמות 21:22), which says the striker shall be fined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof from step 6 by showing the impossible result of the opposite view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יונתן בן שאול's rule that a רודף who could be stopped by a limb may not be killed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fine for the fetus in the פסוק, which can only apply if the striker is not liable to death

steps.title: Perhaps the death and the payment are owed to different people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the striker could pay even if he is liable to death, because the death is for the man and the payment is for the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps here it is different, since the death penalty is on account of this person and the payment is on account of that person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to push back against the proof. Maybe the rule 'liable to death, so exempt from paying' does not apply here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His death liability comes from attacking the man he was fighting. His payment comes from hurting the woman. Since these are two different victims, maybe he can be liable for both, and then the פסוק proves nothing about רבי יונתן בן שאול.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different here,
since the death is on account of this one
phrases.notes: He is liable to death for chasing the man he was fighting with.

phrases.english: and the payment is on account of that one.
phrases.notes: The payment is for the woman he hit by accident.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 7 by limiting the exemption rule to a case of one victim.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the פסוק to רבי יונתן בן שאול's rule
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes that liability to death exempts from payment even when the payment is owed to a different person.

steps.title: רבא: a רודף who breaks anyone's vessels is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there is no difference, citing רבא: a רודף who breaks vessels belonging to the victim or to anyone else is exempt because he is liable to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no difference, as רבא said: A רודף who was chasing another person and broke vessels, whether they belonged to the victim or to anyone else, is exempt. Why? Because he is liable with his life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the pushback from step 8. It brings רבא to show that being liable to death exempts a person from paying even a different person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling covers vessels belonging to anyone at all, not only the victim's. So the exemption applies even when the money is owed to someone other than the one he is chasing. Step 8's distinction fails, and the proof for רבי יונתן בן שאול stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A pursuer chasing someone to kill him
He is liable with his life

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people. The רודף is the attacker doing the chasing, and the נרדף is the victim running away.

phrases.english: There is no difference,
as רבא said:
A pursuer who was chasing after another person,
and broke vessels,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁל נִרְדׇּף וּבֵין שֶׁל כׇּל אָדָם – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: whether those of the pursued or those of anyone else, is exempt.
What is the reason? He is liable with his life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 8 and restores the proof from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: Liability to death exempts from payment even toward a third party
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling about a רודף who breaks anyone's vessels
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the exemption is not limited to the victim. Any payment caused by the same act is cancelled.

steps.title: רבא: when the victim breaks vessels while running away
steps.stepSummary: A נרדף who breaks the רודף's vessels is exempt. If he breaks anyone else's vessels, he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a נרדף who broke vessels: if they belonged to the רודף, he is exempt; if they belonged to anyone else, he must pay. He is exempt for the רודף's vessels, so that the רודף's money should not be dearer to him than his own body. He must pay for anyone else's, because he saved himself with someone else's money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's teaching continues with the other side of the chase: the victim who breaks things while running away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The victim may even injure the רודף's body to save himself, so he surely does not pay for the רודף's belongings. A bystander did nothing wrong, though. If the victim saved his own life using a bystander's property, he must pay that person back.

keyTerms.meaning: Dearer to him than his own body
He saves himself with another person's property

steps.whatToRemember: A רודף never pays for what he breaks during the chase, because he is liable to death. The נרדף does not pay for the רודף's things, but he does pay a bystander whose things he broke while saving himself.

phrases.english: And a pursued person who broke vessels:
if they belonged to the pursuer, he is exempt;
if they belonged to anyone else, he is liable.
For the pursuer's vessels he is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא מָמוֹנוֹ חָבִיב עָלָיו מִגּוּפוֹ.
phrases.english: so that his property should not be dearer to him than his body.
phrases.notes: 'His' means the pursuer. The victim could even hurt the pursuer's body, so his things are surely not protected.

phrases.english: For anyone else's vessels he is liable,
because he saves himself with another person's property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's statement from step 9, moving from the רודף to the נרדף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נרדף is exempt for breaking the רודף's vessels but must pay for a bystander's vessels, since he saved himself at someone else's expense.

steps.title: The rescuer who breaks vessels is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבא's third case: a person chasing the רודף to save the victim is exempt for any vessels he breaks, no matter whose they are.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone chased the רודף to save the victim, and he broke vessels belonging to the רודף, to the victim, or to anyone else, he does not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the last case in his list about broken vessels. This time it is the rescuer, and he is fully exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compare the earlier cases. The רודף is exempt because he is liable to death. The נרדף pays for other people's vessels because he saved himself with their property. The rescuer is exempt even for other people's vessels, which is more generous than the rule for the victim himself.

keyTerms.meaning: exempt, does not have to pay

phrases.aramaic: וְרוֹדֵף שֶׁהָיָה רוֹדֵף אַחַר רוֹדֵף לְהַצִּילוֹ,
phrases.english: And a chaser who was chasing after a pursuer to save him,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the victim: the rescuer chases the attacker to save the person being attacked.

phrases.english: and he broke the vessels –

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁל רוֹדֵף, בֵּין שֶׁל נִרְדׇּף,
phrases.english: whether those of the pursuer, or those of the pursued,
or those of any person – he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרוֹדֵף שֶׁהָיָה רוֹדֵף אַחַר רוֹדֵף לְהַצִּילוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third case in רבא's list, following the רודף (step 9) and the נרדף (step 10).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rescuer who breaks anyone's vessels while chasing the רודף is exempt.

steps.title: Why the rescuer is exempt: so people will still rescue
steps.stepSummary: The rescuer's exemption is not strict law. It is a rule made so that people will not hold back from saving others.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not the strict law. If you did not say this, nobody would ever save his friend from a רודף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the rescuer's exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By strict law the rescuer should pay, at least as much as the victim himself does. But if rescuers had to pay for damage, people would be scared to help. So חז"ל exempted them to keep rescue happening.

keyTerms.meaning: not from strict law (a rule made by חז"ל)
from the hand of the pursuer

steps.whatToRemember: The רודף is exempt because he is liable to death. The נרדף pays others but not the רודף. The rescuer is exempt from everyone, as a special rule to encourage rescue.

phrases.english: And this is not from strict law,
for if you do not say so,
it would turn out that you have no person
who saves his fellow from the hand of the pursuer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא מִן הַדִּין, שֶׁאִם אִי אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the ruling in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rescuer's exemption is a rabbinic rule made so that people will not avoid saving others.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: chasing an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of people who are not stopped by being killed. It starts with one who chases an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: but one who chases an animal [is not stopped by killing him].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה. This is a setup for the ברייתות that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits the right to kill a רודף to cases where a person is harmed. Sins against Heaven, like chasing an animal, עבודה זרה or חילול שבת, are not on the list. The next ברייתות will argue about this.

phrases.english: But one who chases after an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of broken vessels and returns to the משנה's list of exceptions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Per the משנה, one who chases an animal (and similar sinners) is not stopped at the cost of his life.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: kill to stop עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says one may kill someone to stop him from worshipping idols. He learns it with a קל וחומר from the case of נערה המאורסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: one who worships idols may be stopped even at the cost of his life. This is a קל וחומר: if we may kill to stop harm to an ordinary person, then surely we may kill to stop harm to ה׳'s honor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that disagrees with the משנה. It adds עבודה זרה to the cases where we may kill to stop the sinner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר goes like this. If we may kill to stop the shaming of a person, then the shaming of Heaven, which is more serious, should be at least as strong. That would include עבודה זרה among the cases where killing to prevent the sin is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
he may be stopped (saved from sinning) at the cost of his life
a logical argument from a lighter case to a heavier one
damage or shame to an ordinary person
damage or shame to the One Above

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
One who worships idols
may be saved [from the sin] at the cost of his life,
from a kal vachomer.
Now if for the shaming of an ordinary person
phrases.notes: This means the attacked נערה from the משנה. We may kill her attacker to stop him.

phrases.english: he may be stopped at the cost of his life,
for the shaming of the One Above, all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a תנא who disagrees with the משנה's exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון בן יוחי, one may kill an idol worshipper to stop him, learned by קל וחומר.

steps.title: Can we punish based on logic alone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: we usually do not give punishments based on a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we punish based on a קל וחומר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the method רבי שמעון בן יוחי used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A well-known rule says אין עונשין מן הדין. A punishment cannot come from a logical argument alone; it needs a clear פסוק. Killing the idol worshipper is a very severe consequence, so learning it from a קל וחומר seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: but is it so that...? (a challenging question)
we punish based on a logical argument

phrases.english: But do we punish based on a logical derivation?!
phrases.notes: Here "הדין" means the קל וחומר argument, not "the law."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's use of a קל וחומר to allow killing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The accepted rule is that punishments are not learned from a קל וחומר.

steps.title: He holds that we do punish from logic
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי שמעון בן יוחי holds that we may punish based on a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that we do punish based on a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון בן יוחי simply holds the other view about this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed everyone agrees that we do not punish from a קל וחומר. The answer shows that this is a debate, and רבי שמעון בן יוחי is on the side that allows it. So his ruling makes sense within his own view.

phrases.english: He holds: we do punish based on a logical derivation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The answer places the opinion inside a known debate.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees we do not punish from a קל וחומר, so the derivation fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון בן יוחי holds עונשין מן הדין, so his קל וחומר works.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: kill to stop חילול שבת
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says one may kill someone to stop him from breaking שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון says: one who breaks שבת may be stopped even at the cost of his life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that goes further and adds חילול שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This also disagrees with the משנה, which does not allow killing to stop חילול שבת. The next step will explain how רבי אלעזר learns this.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
One who desecrates Shabbat
may be stopped at the cost of his life.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא that extends רבי שמעון בן יוחי's idea to שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר בן רבי שמעון, one may kill a person to stop him from breaking שבת.

steps.title: How רבי אלעזר learns it: his father plus a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר agrees with his father that we punish from a קל וחומר. He then links שבת to עבודה זרה through the shared word "חילול."
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like his father, who said we punish from a קל וחומר. And שבת is learned from עבודה זרה through the word "desecration" that appears by both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי אלעזר's ruling comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two steps. First, his father's קל וחומר allows killing to stop עבודה זרה. Second, a גזירה שוה on the word "חילול" carries that law over to שבת.

phrases.english: He holds like his father,
who said: we punish based on a logical derivation.
And Shabbat is learned
through "desecration" "desecration" from idol worship.
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה. The same word "desecration" is used for both sins, so the law of one is applied to the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כַּאֲבוּהּ, דְּאָמַר: עוֹנְשִׁין מִן הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source for the ruling in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the source through a shared view plus a גזירה שוה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It is unclear how שבת could be added, since the קל וחומר only spoke about עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר covers עבודה זרה, and the shared word "חילול" brings שבת along.

steps.title: The vote in לוד: which sins require giving up one's life
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק that the חכמים voted in לוד. For any sin, a person forced to sin should sin rather than be killed. The exceptions are עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים voted and decided in the attic of בית נתזה in לוד. For every sin in the Torah, if someone is told "sin or be killed," he should sin and not be killed. The exceptions are עבודה זרה, forbidden relations, and murder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings the famous ruling about when a person must give up his life rather than sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that saving a life comes before almost every מצוה. Only three sins are so severe that a person must die rather than do them. The גמרא will go on to discuss where each of these three exceptions comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: he should sin and not be killed

steps.whatToRemember: For any sin, a person forced to sin should sin rather than die. The exceptions are עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים, where he must be killed rather than sin.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier ברייתות. Those asked whether WE may kill a sinner to stop him. This ruling asks whether a person must let HIMSELF be killed rather than sin.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source in הלכה for the rule of יהרג ואל יעבור.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
They voted and concluded
in the upper room of the house of Nitza in Lod,
regarding all transgressions in the Torah:
if they say to a person,
"Transgress and you will not be killed" –
he should transgress and not be killed,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מֵעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְגִילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים.
phrases.english: except for idol worship, forbidden relations, and bloodshed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק: נִימְנוּ וְגָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from killing a sinner to stop him to giving up one's own life rather than sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For any sin a person should transgress rather than be killed, except עבודה זרה, גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי ישמעאל says one may worship idols to save his life
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים could say one must die rather than worship עבודה זרה. רבי ישמעאל learns from 'וחי בהם' that a person should worship and not be killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that a person may not worship idols to save his life? A ברייתא teaches the opposite. רבי ישמעאל said: How do we know that if someone is told 'Worship idols or be killed,' he should worship and not be killed? Because the פסוק says 'and he shall live by them.' The מצוות are for living, not for dying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ruling from לוד in step 19 by quoting a ברייתא. In it רבי ישמעאל allows worshipping עבודה זרה to save one's life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 listed עבודה זרה as one of the three sins where a person must die rather than sin. רבי ישמעאל uses the פסוק 'וחי בהם' to say the מצוות were given so a person can live by them. That would include עבודה זרה. So the two views seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? This opens a challenge from an outside source.
'And he shall live by them.' The מצוות are meant for living.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ישמעאל is not saying עבודה זרה is a light sin. He is only saying that the rule of 'die rather than sin' does not apply to it when done in private.

phrases.english: And idol worship, one may not [do it to save his life]?
phrases.notes: This refers to the vote in לוד from step 19, which said one must die rather than worship idols.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yishmael said:
From where do we know that if they said to a person
"Worship idols and you will not be killed,"
from where do we know that he should worship and not be killed?
The verse teaches: "And he shall live by them"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:5

phrases.english: and not that he should die by them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling from לוד in step 19 about עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 19 that one must be killed rather than worship עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל uses 'וחי בהם' to permit worshipping idols to save one's life. That contradicts the ruling from לוד.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: in public one must die
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל's ברייתא limits his permission. In public a person must be killed rather than worship idols, because of 'ולא תחללו את שם קדשי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a person may worship idols even in public to save his life. So the פסוק says: 'Do not profane My holy name, and I will be sanctified.' In public he must give up his life.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and adds a limit to רבי ישמעאל's rule. The permission applies only in private, not in public. The challenge from step 20 still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל agrees that in public one must die, because worshipping idols there is a חילול השם. But in private he still allows it. That is the part that clashes with the vote in לוד, which made no difference between private and public for עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (a wrong idea the ברייתא is about to reject).
In public, in front of many people.
'And I will be sanctified,' the source for קידוש השם.

phrases.english: One might think [he may worship] even in public?
The verse teaches:
"Do not profane My holy name
and I will be sanctified."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:32

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא used in the challenge. It limits רבי ישמעאל's permission to private settings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling from לוד in step 19 about עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even with the public exception, רבי ישמעאל still allows idol worship in private to save a life. That contradicts the ruling from לוד.

steps.title: Answer: the חכמים followed רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חכמים in לוד ruled like רבי אליעזר. He bases himself on the פסוק 'ואהבת את ה׳ אלהיך בכל לבבך ובכל נפשך ובכל מאדך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those חכמים ruled like רבי אליעזר. A ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר quotes the פסוק: 'And you shall love ה׳ your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the חכמים in לוד held like רבי אליעזר, not like רבי ישמעאל. It begins quoting רבי אליעזר's ברייתא to set up his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a real מחלוקת between תנאים. רבי ישמעאל permits idol worship in private to save one's life. רבי אליעזר requires a person to give up his life. The חכמים in לוד followed רבי אליעזר, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Who said [it] like the view of.
'And you shall love,' from קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: They said [their ruling] according to Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the חכמים who voted in לוד back in step 19.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"And you shall love ה׳ your God

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל לְבָבְךָ וּבְכׇל נַפְשְׁךָ וּבְכׇל מְאֹדֶךָ״.
phrases.english: with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might."
phrases.notes: דברים 6:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 20-21. It ties the vote in לוד to a different תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ruling to a different תנא (a מחלוקת תנאים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling from לוד seemed to contradict an accepted ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חכמים followed רבי אליעזר, who requires giving up one's life rather than worshipping idols, even in private.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר asks: why both 'soul' and 'might'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks why the פסוק needs both 'בכל נפשך' and 'בכל מאדך'. Each one seems to make the other unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק already says 'with all your soul,' why does it also say 'with all your might'? And if it says 'with all your might,' why does it also say 'with all your soul'?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside his ברייתא, רבי אליעזר raises a question about extra words in the פסוק. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'נפשך' means giving up your life, and 'מאדך' means giving up your money. If you must give your life, surely you must give your money. So 'מאדך' seems extra. And if the פסוק stresses money, why mention life at all?

keyTerms.meaning: With all your soul. Even if it costs your life.
With all your might. Here it means all your money and possessions.
Why was it said? Asks what an extra phrase in a פסוק comes to teach.

phrases.english: If it is said "with all your soul,"
why is it said "with all your might"?
And if it is said "with all your might,"
why is it said "with all your soul"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם נֶאֱמַר ״בְּכׇל נַפְשְׁךָ״, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר ״בְּכׇל מְאֹדֶךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אליעזר's ברייתא. It questions the wording of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק needs both phrases when each seems to cover the other.

steps.title: Both phrases are needed for different kinds of people
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that people differ. For one who values his body more, the פסוק says 'בכל נפשך'. For one who values his money more, it says 'בכל מאדך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people care more about their body than their money. For them the פסוק says 'with all your soul.' Other people care more about their money than their body. For them the פסוק says 'with all your might.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his own question. This finishes the proof that the חכמים in לוד relied on him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase speaks to a different type of person, so neither is extra. Since 'בכל נפשך' demands loving ה׳ even at the cost of one's life, one must die rather than worship idols. That is true even in private, which is exactly the ruling from לוד.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת. רבי ישמעאל says one may worship idols in private to save his life ('וחי בהם'), but must die in public. רבי אליעזר says one must give up his life ('בכל נפשך'). The ruling from לוד follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that עבודה זרה is one of the sins where a person must die rather than sin, even in private.

phrases.english: If you have a person
whose body is more precious to him than his money,
for this it is said "with all your soul."
And if you have a person
whose money is more precious to him than his body,
for this it is said "with all your might."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם יֵשׁ לְךָ אָדָם שֶׁגּוּפוֹ חָבִיב עָלָיו מִמָּמוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23. It completes רבי אליעזר's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each phrase is aimed at a different type of person, so both are needed. 'בכל נפשך' requires giving up one's life for ה׳.

steps.title: The source for forbidden relations and murder is רבי's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: For גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים, the rule of dying rather than sinning comes from רבי. He quotes the פסוק about the נערה המאורסה that compares her case to murder.
steps.simpleTranslation: Forbidden relations and bloodshed are learned like רבי. A ברייתא teaches: רבי says, 'For as when a man rises against his neighbor and kills him, so is this matter.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its answer from Step 22. עבודה זרה came from רבי אליעזר, and now it gives the source for the other two sins: a teaching of רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is talking about a betrothed girl who was attacked, yet it suddenly mentions a murderer. That surprising comparison is what רבי will use to learn his rules.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, who compiled the משנה
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Forbidden relations and bloodshed,
are learned like רבי.
As it was taught: רבי says:
"For as when a man rises against his neighbor
and kills him,
so is this matter."
phrases.notes: דברים 22:26. The פסוק is about a betrothed girl who was attacked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in Step 22 by giving the source for the remaining two sins.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ruling to a known Tannaitic source
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule for גילוי עריות and שפיכות דמים follows רבי's reading of the פסוק.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק mention a murderer?
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks what we are meant to learn from bringing up a murderer in the case of the betrothed girl.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did we learn from a murderer?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי asks why the פסוק mentions murder at all. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have spoken about the girl alone. Since the Torah added a comparison to murder, רבי assumes it was put there to teach something.

phrases.english: And what did we learn from a murderer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purpose of the comparison in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the comparison to a murderer teaches.

steps.title: First direction: a murderer may be stopped by killing him
steps.stepSummary: The murder case teaches about the girl, and it also learns from her. Just as one may kill the attacker to save the girl, one may kill a would-be murderer to save the victim.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, this came to teach and turns out to learn. It compares a murderer to a betrothed girl: just as with a betrothed girl one may save her at the cost of the attacker's life, so too with a murderer one may save the victim at the cost of the murderer's life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers that the comparison works both ways. Here is the first direction: the rule of killing the attacker passes from the girl's case to the murderer's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already says that the girl may be saved by killing her attacker. Because the פסוק links the two cases, the same rescue rule now applies to someone chasing another person to kill him.

keyTerms.meaning: Came to teach and ends up learning: a comparison that works in both directions
Compares (a הֶקֵּשׁ, a link the Torah makes between two cases)
To save by taking the attacker's life

phrases.english: Now, this came to teach
phrases.notes: The murder case was brought in to teach about the girl.

phrases.english: and turns out to learn as well.
It compares a murderer to a betrothed girl:

phrases.aramaic: מָה נַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה – נִיתָּן לְהַצִּילוֹ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: just as with a betrothed girl, one may save at the cost of his life,
phrases.notes: Literally "save him with his life." He means you may kill the attacker to stop him.

phrases.english: so too with a murderer,
one may save at the cost of his life.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעַתָּה, הֲרֵי זֶה בָּא לְלַמֵּד וְנִמְצָא לָמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question by explaining the first direction of the comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The murderer case learns from the girl's case: a would-be murderer may be killed to save his victim.

steps.title: Second direction: the girl must die rather than sin
steps.stepSummary: The comparison also runs the other way. Just as one must be killed rather than murder, the betrothed girl must be killed rather than allow the forbidden act.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it compares a betrothed girl to a murderer: just as with a murderer one must be killed and not sin, so too a betrothed girl must be killed and not sin.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the second direction of רבי's comparison. The rule יהרג ואל יעבור passes from murder to forbidden relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the actual source the גמרא needed for גילוי עריות. It assumes that for murder the rule of dying rather than sinning is already known, which raises the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him be killed and not transgress

steps.whatToRemember: רבי's היקש works both ways. From the girl, a would-be murderer may be killed to save the victim. From murder, one must die rather than commit גילוי עריות.

phrases.english: And it compares a betrothed girl to a murderer:
just as with a murderer, one must be killed and not transgress,
phrases.notes: This means someone who is forced to murder. He must let himself be killed instead.

phrases.aramaic: אַף נַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה תֵּהָרֵג וְאַל תַּעֲבוֹר.
phrases.english: so too a betrothed girl must be killed and not transgress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second, reverse direction of the same comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: גילוי עריות has the rule of יהרג ואל יעבור, learned from murder.

steps.title: How do we know the rule for murder itself?
steps.stepSummary: The girl's rule was learned from murder. So the גמרא asks where we know that one must die rather than murder.
steps.simpleTranslation: The murderer himself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the comparison assumed the rule for murder. Now it asks for that rule's own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot learn the girl's case from murder unless murder's rule is already established. So the גמרא needs a separate basis for יהרג ואל יעבור in murder.

phrases.english: The murderer himself, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the base rule that Step 28 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that one must be killed rather than commit murder.

steps.title: It is simple logic
steps.stepSummary: No פסוק is needed. The rule for murder comes from logic.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logical reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule for murder needs no פסוק because it is plain common sense. The next step shows that logic through a story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סברא is a source just as strong as a פסוק. Here the logic is that you may not save your own life by taking someone else's.

phrases.english: It is logical reasoning,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule for murder is based on logic, not on a פסוק.

steps.title: רבה's ruling: who says your blood is redder?
steps.stepSummary: A man was ordered to kill someone or be killed. רבה told him to let himself be killed, because no one can say his own life is worth more than the other person's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone came before רבה and said: The lord of my town told me, 'Go kill so-and-so, and if not, I will kill you.' רבה said to him: Let them kill you, and do not kill. Who says your blood is redder? Maybe that man's blood is redder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the logic behind the rule for murder. רבה rules that the man must die rather than kill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you kill to save yourself, you are treating your life as worth more than the victim's. Since no one can know that, you have no right to trade his life for yours, so you must not kill.

keyTerms.meaning: The lord of my town, a local ruler

steps.whatToRemember: The rule for murder needs no פסוק. It comes from logic: you may not save your own life by taking another's, because no one can say whose blood is redder.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה's logic is about trading one innocent life for another. It does not stop you from killing an attacker to save his victim. That was allowed in Step 27.

phrases.english: As a certain man came before רבה

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲמַר לִי מָרֵי דּוּרַאי
phrases.english: and said to him: The lord of my town told me,
"Go kill so-and-so,
and if not, I will kill you."
He said to him: Let them kill you, and do not kill.

phrases.aramaic: מִי יֵימַר דִּדְמָא דִּידָךְ סוּמָּק טְפֵי?
phrases.english: Who says that your blood is redder?

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא דְּמָא דְּהוּא גַּבְרָא סוּמָּק טְפֵי.
phrases.english: Perhaps that man's blood is redder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and spells out the סברא given in Step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one must be killed rather than commit murder.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבה's ruling and his reasoning: who says your blood is redder?
steps.whyThisMatters: This סברא is the base for the whole chain. Murder's rule comes from logic, and through רבי's היקש it carries over to גילוי עריות.

steps.title: In a time of persecution, one must die even for a minor מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the rule 'sin rather than die' applies only when there is no persecution. In a time of persecution, one must die rather than break even a minor מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: The rule that a person may sin to save his life was only taught for a time without persecution. But in a time of persecution, even for a minor מצוה, he must be killed and not sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main rule of the סוגיא (for most sins, sin rather than die) and limits it. רב דימי says the rule does not apply during a time of persecution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule was: for every sin except the three big ones, a person sins and lives. רבי יוחנן now says this is true only in normal times. When the government is trying to force Jews to give up their religion, a person must give up his life even for a small מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings)
They only taught this rule in the case of...
A time of religious persecution, when rulers try to make Jews abandon the Torah
He must be killed and not transgress

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this cancels the earlier rule. In normal times the earlier rule still stands: for most sins, one sins and lives. רב דימי only adds an exception for times of persecution.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that whether one must give up his life depends on the situation, not only on which sin is involved.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
They only taught this
phrases.notes: 'This' is the earlier rule: for most sins, a person should sin rather than be killed.

phrases.english: when it is not a time of persecution.
But in a time of persecution,
even for a minor מצוה,
he must be killed and not transgress.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the murder and betrothed girl discussion and goes back to the main rule of 'sin rather than die', adding a limit to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule 'sin rather than die' applies only when there is no persecution. In a time of persecution, one must die rather than break even a minor מצוה.

steps.title: Even without persecution, one must die for a minor מצוה in public
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי יוחנן a further limit. Even with no persecution, the rule 'sin rather than die' applies only in private. In public, one must die rather than break even a minor מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: Even when it is not a time of persecution, they only said the rule for a private setting. But in public, even for a minor מצוה, he must be killed and not sin.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report of רבי יוחנן's teaching adds another limit. Even in normal times, if the sin is demanded in public, a person must die rather than sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי gave one exception: a time of persecution. רבין adds a second: even in normal times, the permission to sin and live applies only in private. When the demand is public, even a minor מצוה requires giving up one's life.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said it in the case of...

steps.whatToRemember: There are two exceptions to 'sin rather than die' for ordinary מצוות: (1) a time of persecution (שעת השמד), and (2) even in normal times, a public demand (פרהסיא). In both cases one must die even for a minor מצוה.

phrases.english: When Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even when it is not a time of persecution,
they only said it for a private setting.
phrases.notes: 'It' means the permission to sin in order to stay alive.

phrases.english: But in public,
even for a minor מצוה,
he must be killed and not transgress.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת הַשְּׁמָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב דימי's report. It agrees about times of persecution and adds that even in normal times, a public demand also requires giving up one's life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with no persecution, the permission to sin and live applies only in private. In public, one must die rather than break even a minor מצוה.

steps.title: What counts as a minor מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'minor מצוה' means in these rulings and introduces the answer of רבא בר רב יצחק in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a 'minor מצוה'? רבא בר רב יצחק said that רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of מצוה the phrase 'minor מצוה' refers to. It then introduces who will answer, setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רב דימי and רבין used the phrase 'even a minor מצוה', but neither explained it. The גמרא wants to know the exact limit, since a person must give up his life for it in these cases. The answer itself follows right after this line.

phrases.english: What is a minor מצוה?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Yitzchak said that Rav said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term 'minor מצוה' used in both of the previous reports.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of 'minor מצוה', meaning which kind of מצוה a person must die for in a time of persecution or in public.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer, from רבא בר רב יצחק in the name of רב, comes in the next part of the text.
